answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks, an agent haven managing crystal or lotus exchanges requires verifiable delay functions. Each agent must submit sequential, non-parallelizable hash evaluations bound to its public key before issuing actions. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of elapsed wall-clock time and dedicated compute threads per identity. However, adversaries deploying customized ASIC hardware can compute these delays faster, undermining parity for standard edge agents.
